quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only while making the move, not before.
Not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb so other drivers know your plan.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block the vehicle.
Do everything you can to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal to tell the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to let an emergency vehicle pass. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to create an open path for the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Stop a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. Never swerve across lanes at the last second to catch your exit. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and check your blind spot by looking over your left shoulder when passing left.
See both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before you change lanes to pass. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your original lane.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others to go ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give the right-of-way to any blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. Be ready to stop to prevent injury or danger.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you are not the driver.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry any open alcohol in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container in the driver or passenger area of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: Which statement about bad weather driving is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain or fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather suddenly changes, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog. Watch for cars behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. You should:

options.text: Move to another lane if safe to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if safe to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging and you have two or more lanes, make room for entering vehicles. If the lane next to you is empty, move over.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you can see less than 500 feet ahead. Use low beams, not high beams. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Take your foot off the gas and let your vehicle slow down before you brake.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to slow your vehicle. Then press the brake pedal steadily. Your brake lights will turn on and your vehicle will stop smoothly.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: An octagonal (8-sided) sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop when you see a red octagonal sign.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. Cars from both directions must stay in their own lane.

questions.question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to:
questions.explanation: Tired driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. Stop driving as soon as you feel tired.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the full lane width, just like any other vehicle on the road.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects how you judge speed and distance. Alcohol lowers inhibitions and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: First, turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: A person's ability to drive can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You are driving when it starts to sleet or snow. You should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: In snow and sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clean. Leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead because slippery roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, you should slow down:

options.text: In the middle of the curve.
Only if you see traffic coming.

questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Driving too fast can cause your tires to lose grip on the road.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing any railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted on the road:
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They mark where you must stop.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Your body breaks it down more quickly.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a school zone is ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, you should:
questions.explanation: In a crash, stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. If anyone is injured, call 911. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or damage over $1,000 (or over $200 to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?
questions.explanation: Do not pass in a tunnel, on a bridge, or in an underpass. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped warning signs have black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes very slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Which of the following puts distracted drivers at greater risk of a crash?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player while driving is dangerous and increases crash risk. This includes hands-free phones.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires can cause which of these problems?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning harder, increase stopping distance, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake right away. Gradually slow down and gently apply the brakes before pulling off the road.

questions.question: What must you present to get a New Jersey driver license or non-driver ID card?
questions.explanation: All applicants must show proof of age, identity, and legal U.S. presence. You must also provide proof of address and your Social Security number (or an exemption letter if you cannot get a number).

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both your side and rearview mirrors. Then glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow (to the left in this case). Multiple chevron signs may appear throughout the curve.

questions.question: Where should you remove snow and ice from your vehicle?
questions.explanation: The law requires you to remove all snow and ice from your vehicle before driving. You may be fined if you do not follow this rule.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no traffic is crossing.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. You must stop and treat them like stop signs.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. Strong feelings like worry, anger, or sadness can reduce your focus. Stress lowers your concentration. It is better to wait to drive than to drive while emotionally upset.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection and the traffic light turns yellow, your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Before starting your engine, you should:

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt before starting your engine. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Passing other vehicles is prohibited:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass other vehicles on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid on sharp turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal your left turn three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. You need to focus fully on driving. Any other activity can be a dangerous distraction.
